pains: My commute is so loud I can't hear my own podcast, and I keep turning it up until my ears hurt.
My apartment is never quiet. Someone's always drilling, or the neighbors are loud, and I can't focus on work.
Big over-ear headphones are a pain to carry. They don't fit in my bag and I feel ridiculous wearing them on the train.
My earbuds die halfway through the day and I'm hunting for a charger at 3pm.
I'm sick of cheap earbuds that let in every sound and still make me feel like I'm shouting over the noise.
desires: I just want real quiet on the train without lugging around giant headphones.
I want earbuds that last a full workday so I'm not watching the battery.
I want something that slides into my pocket and doesn't make my bag heavier.
I want to put them in and have the noise just drop away so I can focus.
I want gear that looks clean and understated, not like a gadget.
objections: Noise cancelling in earbuds is usually just okay. Does it actually block anything?
Eight hours sounds fine, but I want to know it'll get me through my whole day.
Earbuds always get uncomfortable after an hour for me.
I don't want to spend money on another pair that ends up in a drawer.
Matte finishes look nice, but I don't want something that gets scuffed up in my pocket.
proof_points: Active noise cancellation to quiet the noise around you.
Up to 8 hours of playback per charge.
Comes with a pocket charging case, so you can take it anywhere.
Matte graphite finish that keeps the look understated.
Small earbuds instead of bulky headphones, with a case that fits in your pocket.
